# PIGSTY

> Pigsty, the FOSS PostgreSQL RDS, self-host PG like a pro, with Monitoring, HA, PITR, IAC, 12 kernels and 576 packaged PG extensions

## Site index

- [Home page](https://pigsty.io/index.md)
- [Docs](https://pigsty.io/docs/index.md)
- [Extensions](https://pigsty.io/ext/): Extensions are the soul of PostgreSQL. Pigsty builds, packages, collects, and integrates 576 PG ecosystem extensions for out-of-the-box use.
- [Blog](https://pigsty.io/blog/index.md): Articles about Pigsty, cloud computing, database industry, AI/Agent, and notes on PostgreSQL development, administration, and internals
- [Services](https://pigsty.io/price/index.md): Pigsty offers flexible service plans, from free open source to enterprise support, tailored to your needs

## Documentation index

- [Get Started](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/index.md): Deploy Pigsty single-node version on your laptop/cloud server, access DB and Web UI
  - [Quick Start](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/install/index.md): Get started with Pigsty—complete single-node install on a fresh Linux host!
  - [Docker](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/docker/index.md): Spin up Pigsty in Docker containers for quick testing on macOS/Windows
  - [Web UI](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/webui/index.md): Explore Pigsty's Web graphical management interface, Grafana dashboards, and how to access them via domain names and HTTPS.
  - [Use PG](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/pgsql/index.md): Get started with PostgreSQL—connect using CLI and graphical clients
  - [Customize](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/config/index.md): Express your infra and clusters with declarative config files
  - [Playbook](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/playbook/index.md): Use Ansible playbooks to deploy and manage Pigsty clusters
  - [Offline](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/offline/index.md): Install Pigsty in air-gapped env using offline packages
  - [Slim](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/slim/index.md): Install only HA PostgreSQL clusters with minimal dependencies
  - [Security Recommendations](https://pigsty.io/docs/setup/security/index.md): Basic security checks for quick-start and single-node deployments.
- [Deployment](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/index.md): Multi-node, high-availability Pigsty deployment for production environments.
  - [Prod Install](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/install/index.md): How to install Pigsty on Linux hosts for production?
  - [Preparation](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/prepare/index.md): Production deployment preparation including hardware, nodes, disks, network, VIP, domain, software, and filesystem requirements.
  - [Arch Planning](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/planning/index.md): How many nodes? Which modules need HA? How to plan based on available resources and requirements?
  - [Admin Setup](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/admin/index.md): Admin user, sudo, SSH, accessibility verification, and firewall configuration
  - [Sandbox](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/sandbox/index.md): 4-node sandbox environment for learning, testing, and demonstration
  - [Vagrant](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/vagrant/index.md): Create local virtual machine environment with Vagrant
  - [Terraform](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/terraform/index.md): Create virtual machine environment on public cloud with Terraform
  - [Security Considerations](https://pigsty.io/docs/deploy/security/index.md): Credential, network, authentication, encryption, data protection, and audit checks for production Pigsty deployments.
- [Concepts](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/index.md): Understand Pigsty's core concepts, architecture design, learn how high availability, backup recovery, iac, security works
  - [Expire Failure](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/ha/failure/passive/index.md): Failover path triggered by node crash causing leader lease expiration and cluster election
  - [Infra Cluster](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/model/infra/index.md): Entity-Relationship model for INFRA infrastructure nodes in Pigsty, component composition, and naming conventions.
  - [RPO Trade-offs](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/ha/rpo/index.md): Trade-off analysis for RPO (Recovery Point Objective), finding the optimal balance between availability and data loss.
  - [Crash Failure](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/ha/failure/active/index.md): PostgreSQL primary process crashes while Patroni stays alive and attempts restart, triggering failover after timeout
  - [PGSQL Cluster](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/model/pgsql/index.md): Entity-Relationship model for PostgreSQL clusters in Pigsty, including E-R diagram, entity definitions, and naming conventions.
  - [Etcd Cluster](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/model/etcd/index.md): Entity-Relationship model for ETCD clusters in Pigsty, including E-R diagram, entity definitions, and naming conventions.
  - [Network Partition](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/ha/failure/partition/index.md): Primary loses DCS connectivity, causing lease expiration and triggering split-brain protection and failover
  - [Object Storage Cluster](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/model/minio/index.md): The cluster, instance, and node identity model used when Pigsty's MINIO module deploys Silo.
  - [Redis Cluster](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/model/redis/index.md): Entity-Relationship model for Redis clusters in Pigsty, including E-R diagram, entity definitions, and naming conventions.
  - [Nodes](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/arch/node/index.md): A node is an abstraction of hardware/OS resources—physical machines, bare metal, VMs, or containers/pods.
  - [Infrastructure](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/arch/infra/index.md): Infrastructure module architecture, components, and functionality in Pigsty.
  - [PGSQL Arch](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/arch/pgsql/index.md): PostgreSQL module component interactions and data flow.
  - [RTO Trade-offs](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/ha/rto/index.md): Trade-off analysis for RTO (Recovery Time Objective), finding the optimal balance between recovery speed and false failover risk.
  - [Inventory](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/iac/inventory/index.md): Describe your infrastructure and clusters using declarative configuration files
  - [Mechanism](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/pitr/mechanism/index.md): Snapshots, WAL history, recovery windows, recovery targets, and timelines: the five concepts needed to reason accurately about PostgreSQL PITR.
  - [Architecture](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/pitr/arch/index.md): Pigsty implements PITR with pgBackRest: repository selection, archive flow, scheduling, primary-aware backup execution, performance defaults, and observability.
  - [Configure](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/iac/configure/index.md): Use the configure script to automatically generate recommended configuration files based on your environment.
  - [Parameters](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/iac/parameter/index.md): Fine-tune Pigsty customization using configuration parameters
  - [Tradeoffs](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/pitr/tradeoff/index.md): Repository location determines the failure domain, retention determines the recovery window, and backup frequency shapes restore time. Together they define a backup policy.
  - [Recovery](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/pitr/restore/index.md): Declare the desired pg_pitr recovery target and let pgsql-pitr.yml or pig orchestrate the recovery workflow.
  - [Scenarios](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/pitr/scenarios/index.md): How to choose a recovery target and workflow for accidental DML, dropped objects, defective releases, investigations, and site loss — and why recovery drills must be routine.
  - [Templates](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/iac/template/index.md): Use pre-made configuration templates to quickly generate configuration files adapted to your environment
  - [CMDB](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/iac/cmdb/index.md): Use PostgreSQL as a CMDB metabase to store Ansible inventory.
  - [Monitoring System](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/monitor/index.md): How Pigsty's monitoring system is architected and how monitored targets are automatically managed.
  - [Service Access](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/ha/svc/index.md): Pigsty uses HAProxy to provide service access, with optional pgBouncer for connection pooling, and optional L2 VIP and DNS access.
  - [Security Model](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/sec/level/index.md): Pigsty trust boundaries and defense in depth, with the admin node as a high-trust control plane and a path from the default baseline to production hardening.
  - [Authentication](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/sec/auth/index.md): Pigsty manages PostgreSQL and PgBouncer HBA rules declaratively, combining SCRAM passwords and client certificates to define who may connect and how identity is proven.
  - [Access Control](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/sec/ac/index.md): Pigsty turns least privilege into reusable declarative cluster configuration through a built-in four-tier role model and default privilege templates.
  - [Encrypted Communication](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/sec/ca/index.md): Pigsty provides a self-signed CA that issues certificates and distributes trust for managed components, creating a unified TLS foundation.
  - [Data Security](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/sec/data/index.md): Protect PostgreSQL data integrity, recoverability, confidentiality, and traceability with checksums, backup and PITR, encryption, and audit logs.
  - [Compliance](https://pigsty.io/docs/concept/sec/compliance/index.md): Compliance combines configuration, process, and evidence. This page covers launch hardening, MLPS and SOC 2 control mappings, supply-chain integrity, and vulnerability response.

- [Conf Sample](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/index.md): Batteries-included configuration templates for specific scenarios, with detailed explanations.
  - [Solo Templates](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/_div_solo/index.md)
  - [meta](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/meta/index.md): Default single-node installation template with extensive configuration parameter descriptions
  - [rich](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/rich/index.md): Feature-rich single-node configuration with local software repository, all extensions, Silo backup, and complete examples
  - [slim](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/slim/index.md): Minimal installation template without monitoring infrastructure, installs PostgreSQL directly from internet
  - [fat](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/fat/index.md): Feature-All-Test template, single-node installation of all extensions, builds local repo with PG 14-18 all versions
  - [infra](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/infra/index.md): Only installs observability infrastructure, dedicated template without PostgreSQL and etcd
  - [vibe](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/vibe/index.md): VIBE AI coding sandbox config template, integrating Code-Server, JupyterLab, Claude Code, Codex CLI, and JuiceFS
  - [docker](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/docker/index.md): Pigsty Docker single-node template for quickly bootstrapping Pigsty in containers.
  - [Kernel Templates](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/_div_kernel/index.md)
  - [pgsql](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/pgsql/index.md): Native PostgreSQL kernel with stable support for PostgreSQL 14 to 18 and a PG19 Beta evaluation option
  - [pg19](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/pg19/index.md): Single-node PostgreSQL 19 Beta evaluation template with the PGDG Beta repository and default backup capabilities
  - [mssql](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/mssql/index.md): Babelfish template pinned to a PostgreSQL 17-compatible kernel with SQL Server protocol and T-SQL support
  - [polar](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/polar/index.md): PolarDB for PostgreSQL kernel, provides Aurora-style storage-compute separation capability
  - [cloudberry](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/cloudberry/index.md): Placeholder for the Cloudberry config template (not yet available).
  - [ivory](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/ivory/index.md): IvorySQL kernel, provides Oracle syntax and PL/SQL compatibility
  - [agens](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/agens/index.md): AgensGraph kernel template with property graph model and Cypher query support
  - [pgedge](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/pgedge/index.md): pgEdge kernel template for distributed multi-master PostgreSQL in edge scenarios
  - [mysql](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/mysql/index.md): OpenHalo kernel, provides MySQL protocol and syntax compatibility
  - [pgtde](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/pgtde/index.md): Percona PostgreSQL kernel, provides Transparent Data Encryption (pg_tde) capability
  - [oriole](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/oriole/index.md): OrioleDB kernel, provides bloat-free OLTP enhanced storage engine
  - [Mongo](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/mongo/index.md): Run PostgreSQL in Mongo-compatible mode with DocumentDB and the FerretDB Docker APP.
  - [HA Templates](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/_div_ha/index.md)
  - [ha/simu](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/simu/index.md): 20-node production environment simulation for large-scale deployment testing
  - [ha/octo](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/octo/index.md): Compact eight-node HA simulation with three INFRA nodes, five etcd nodes, eight object-storage nodes, and two PostgreSQL clusters.
  - [ha/full](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/full/index.md): Four-node complete feature demonstration environment with two PostgreSQL clusters, Silo, Redis, etc.
  - [ha/safe](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/safe/index.md): Three-node high-availability and security-hardening configuration example.
  - [ha/trio](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/trio/index.md): Three-node standard HA configuration where PostgreSQL, ETCD, and Silo tolerate one node failure
  - [ha/dual](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/dual/index.md): Two-node configuration, limited HA deployment tolerating specific server failure
  - [ha/citus](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/citus/index.md): 13-node Citus distributed PostgreSQL cluster, 1 coordinator + 5 worker groups with HA
  - [App Templates](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/_div_app/index.md)
  - [supabase](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/supabase/index.md): Self-host Supabase using Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL, an open-source Firebase alternative
  - [app/odoo](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/odoo/index.md): Deploy Odoo open-source ERP system using Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/dify](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/dify/index.md): Deploy Dify AI application development platform using Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/electric](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/electric/index.md): Deploy Electric real-time sync service using Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/maybe](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/maybe/index.md): Deploy Maybe personal finance management system using Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/teable](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/teable/index.md): Deploy Teable open-source Airtable alternative using Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/mattermost](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/mattermost/index.md): Mattermost template for one-click team collaboration deployment with Pigsty PostgreSQL and Docker.
  - [app/registry](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/registry/index.md): Deploy Docker Registry image proxy and private registry using Pigsty
  - [app/insforge](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/insforge/index.md): Deploy the InsForge Backend-as-a-Service platform with Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/hindsight](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/hindsight/index.md): Deploy the Hindsight AI long-term memory service with Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [app/immich](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/immich/index.md): Deploy Immich photo and video management with Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL and VectorChord
  - [app/jumpserver](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/jumpserver/index.md): Deploy the JumpServer open-source bastion host with Pigsty-managed PostgreSQL
  - [Misc Templates](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/_div_misc/index.md)
  - [demo/bare](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/bare/index.md): Minimal readable configuration declaring only INFRA, ETCD, and single-node PostgreSQL
  - [demo/el](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/el/index.md): Configuration template optimized for Enterprise Linux (RHEL/Rocky/Alma)
  - [demo/debian](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/debian/index.md): Configuration template optimized for Debian/Ubuntu
  - [demo/demo](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/demo/index.md): Pigsty public demo site configuration, showcasing SSL certificates, domain exposure, and full extension installation
  - [demo/kernel](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/kernel/index.md): Ten-node PostgreSQL kernel matrix demo configuration
  - [demo/minio](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/minio/index.md): Four-node x four-drive HA S3 object-storage cluster demo; current source defaults to Silo.
  - [demo/redis](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/redis/index.md): Four-node demo of Redis replica, Sentinel, and native Cluster modes
  - [demo/kafka](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/kafka/index.md): Four-node dynamic KRaft example with a plaintext single-node dev cluster and a three-node TLS/SCRAM HA baseline
  - [demo/mysql](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/mysql84/index.md): Native MySQL 8.4 pilot template with a standalone instance and a three-node InnoDB Cluster
  - [build/oss](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/oss/index.md): Pigsty open-source edition offline package build environment configuration
  - [build/dev](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/dev/index.md): Pigsty three-node local build and development configuration
  - [demo/remote](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/remote/index.md): Monitor remote PostgreSQL and cloud RDS with pg_exporter instances on an INFRA node
  - [demo/saas](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/saas/index.md): Legacy single-node SaaS bundle with PostgreSQL, Silo, Redis, and multiple application entrypoints
  - [demo/wool](https://pigsty.io/docs/conf/wool/index.md): Single-node tiny-tuning example for small cloud instances in China
- [Repository](https://pigsty.io/docs/repo/index.md): The APT / DNF repository to deliver PostgreSQL Kernel, Extensions and Infra packages.
  - [PGDG Repo](https://pigsty.io/docs/repo/pgdg/index.md): The official PostgreSQL APT/YUM repository
  - [GPG Key](https://pigsty.io/docs/repo/gpg/index.md): Import the GPG key for Pigsty repository
